title: Plan first: coordinated plan orders the drain; stop at job boundary
summary: Add a planning stage before design/code. Each request is fleshed out (goal, ladder rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, touched paths), and all open items are planned together into one ordered plan with parallel groups. The drain follows that plan instead of strictly oldest first, can be stopped at a job boundary, and the plan-stage audit from n2qb and the order/stop work from vs76 are covered. Audience: the owner and the verifier, who judge by running drain tests.

defaults_applied.how: New plan and stop logic have passing tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
One focused change on plan and drain order; parallel execution deferred.
Criteria check order and stop behavior by running tests.
Alternatives noted in docs/decisions.md or design doc.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: make planning the first stage for every request and replace one-at-a-time oldest-first draining with a coordinated plan, serving the owner who wrote the 2026-10-16 addendum.

Parallel running itself is not implemented; the plan only states which items can run in parallel and in what order, and the drain still runs one job at a time in plan order (execution parallelism is follow-up).
Stop at a job boundary is a stop-file or flag checked between jobs, with a new Stop reason.
Plan order follows ladder priority, then dependencies, then age as tiebreak.
The n2qb audit is delivered as a first slice (stage tracing plus a planning-completeness gate), not a full autonomous role.
I only skimmed the code: drain.rs has Stop with five reasons and QueueView items; no planning module exists. Exact seams may differ.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a drain test with three queued items where a newer item is planned first shows the drain works items in plan order, not oldest first.
Run cargo test: a drain test that requests a stop mid-run shows the loop finishes the current job, starts no further job, and reports a distinct stop reason (not a killed job).

Run cargo test: a plan built from several open items names, for each, goal, ladder rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, and touched paths, and groups items with disjoint touches and no dependency as parallel while ordering dependent items after what they need.
Run cargo test: an item whose plan lacks goal, ladder rung, or acceptance is refused for design or code and reported, so planning cannot be skipped.

The plan-stage audit from n2qb is described: each logged gap (intervention, introspection, rejection, rating) is traced to a stage (reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check), with a check of whether later gaps of that kind fell; if full automation is too large, the remainder is stated as follow-up.
Docs (README, design doc, CHANGELOG) state the planning-first order and how to stop a drain at a job boundary, for an outside reader.
Run cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check: all pass, and no new unused or untested module.
No design work for moving compute to CI is included; it is left for after this lands.

out_of_scope: Moving compute to CI and intelligent routing (design after this lands)
departures: Request spans planning stage, queue ordering, drain stop and audit across several crates, so cost, time and failure odds exceed the reference.
